children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were stronger on Tuesday, closing just short of contract highs as weather concerns in parts of the Prairies and spillover from advances in crude oil provided support.
- November canola was up C$16.60 at C$839.10 per tonne, trading well above its major moving averages.

- The heightened conflict in the Middle East underpinned world crude and vegetable oil markets, with strength in Chicago soyoil and European rapeseed futures contributing to the firmer tone in canola.
- Heavy rains across the Prairies over the weekend added to the strength in canola, as the untimely moisture flooded some fields and raised concerns over potential harvest delays.
- Statistics Canada will release ending stocks estimates for the 2025-26 marketing year on Wednesday. The agency's first production estimates for 2026-27 will be out the following week.
- There were 57,223 contracts traded on Tuesday, which compares with Friday when 39,575 contracts changed hands.
Spreading accounted for 29,236 of the contracts traded.
